blogs.title: A Pancreatic Disease Wearing a Pulmonary Mask
blogs.description: This post would use the case to highlight why pancreatopleural fistula is so often missed: children present with dyspnea, chest pain, and massive recurrent pleural effusions while the true pathology lies below the diaphragm. It would focus on clinical clues that should trigger consideration of a pancreatic source, especially recurrent unilateral or bilateral blood-stained effusions with little to no abdominal symptomatology.

blogs.title: Pleural Fluid Amylase: The Forgotten Test in Recurrent Hemorrhagic Effusion
blogs.description: This post would center on the diagnostic value of sending pleural amylase and lipase in unexplained recurrent exudative or hemorrhagic pleural effusions. It would review the differential diagnosis of amylase-rich pleural fluid, including pancreatopleural fistula, esophageal perforation, malignancy, and tuberculosis mimics, and explain how pancreatic versus salivary amylase patterns can refine the diagnosis.

blogs.title: TB Contact, Mildly Elevated ADA, and the Risk of Anchoring
blogs.description: This post would examine the cognitive errors illustrated by the case: a child with TB exposure and a mildly elevated pleural ADA was empirically started on antitubercular therapy before the true diagnosis emerged. The discussion would explore how anchoring, premature closure, and diagnostic momentum develop in pleural effusion workups, and how repeated history-taking—such as uncovering remote bicycle-handle trauma—can rescue the diagnosis.

blogs.title: CT, MRCP, or ERCP? Imaging Strategy for Suspected Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: This post would compare the roles of CT, MRCP, and ERCP in suspected pancreatopleural fistula. Using the anatomy in this case, it would explain how pancreatic duct disruption leads to retroperitoneal tracking through the diaphragmatic hiatus into the chest, what each imaging test can and cannot show, and how to choose an imaging pathway that balances diagnostic yield with invasiveness in pediatric patients.

blogs.title: How Long Should You Wait? Conservative Management of Pediatric Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: This post would focus on management tensions in a rare disease without robust pediatric guidelines. It would review the rationale and limitations of bowel rest, TPN, octreotide, chest drainage, and enzyme replacement, then discuss when conservative treatment is enough and when to escalate to ERCP with transpapillary stenting or surgery based on duct anatomy, persistent output, and duration of nonresponse.
